scenes.heading: Ratios and rates in problems
scenes.sub: Find one part, and the rest is easy
scenes.say: A choir has four boys for every seven girls, and eighteen more girls than boys. How many singers is that? Today you will crack problems like this with one simple idea: find one part first.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Cordial: 1 part cordial to 4 parts water, any size of part
scenes.science: In a ratio, first find how big one part is
scenes.breaks: Cordial and water use the same unit. A rate, like km per hour, compares different units.
scenes.say: A cordial label says one part cordial to four parts water. A part can be a cup or a bucket. The drink tastes the same as long as every part is the same size. Ratio problems are about finding how big one part is.

scenes.heading: Ways to find one part
points: Know the total: total ÷ all the parts
Know one share: share ÷ its parts
Know a difference: difference ÷ gap in parts
scenes.say: There are three ways to find one part. If you know the total, divide by all the parts. If you know one share, divide by its parts. If you know a difference, divide by the gap in parts.

scenes.heading: When you know a difference
scenes.say: Here are the boys as four boxes and the girls as seven boxes. The girls have three extra boxes, and those are the eighteen extra girls. So one box is six students, and eleven boxes make sixty-six singers.
scenes.caption: Boys are 4 boxes and girls are 7 boxes. The 3 extra boxes are the 18 extra girls. So one box is 6 students, and 11 boxes make 66 singers.

scenes.heading: Linking two ratios
scenes.question: a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 4 : 5. Find a : b : c.
lines: Match b: LCM of 3 and 4 is 12
scenes.say: To link two ratios, make the shared letter match. B is three parts in one and four parts in the other. The lowest common multiple is twelve. So a to b is eight to twelve, b to c is twelve to fifteen, and a to b to c is eight to twelve to fifteen.
scenes.caption: To link two ratios, make the shared letter match. b is 3 parts in one and 4 in the other. The LCM is 12. a : b = 8 : 12, b : c = 12 : 15, so a : b : c = 8 : 12 : 15.

scenes.heading: Speed is a rate
scenes.say: A rate compares different units. Speed is distance divided by time. Change minutes into hours first: thirty minutes is zero point five hours.
scenes.caption: A rate compares different units. Speed = distance ÷ time. Change minutes into hours first: 30 minutes is 0.5 h.

scenes.heading: How long will it take?
scenes.question: A car travels 135 km in 1 h 30 min. At that speed, how long for 210 km?
scenes.say: A car travels one hundred and thirty-five kilometres in one and a half hours. That is ninety kilometres per hour. Two hundred and ten divided by ninety is two and a third hours, which is two hours and twenty minutes.
scenes.caption: A car travels 135 km in 1.5 h: 90 km/h. 210 ÷ 90 = 2 1/3 h, which is 2 h 20 min.

points: Difference in amounts = gap in parts
Link ratios by matching the shared term
Best buy: compare the same amount
scenes.say: Quick recap. Find one part first. A difference in amounts matches the gap in parts. Link ratios by matching the shared term. For best buys, compare the same amount. And speed is distance over time. Now try the practice questions!
